card.title: When does the clock run out?

body.question: Unix time counts seconds since 1 January 1970 and is often stored in a signed 32-bit integer. When does that counter reach its maximum?
body.reveal: A signed 32-bit integer can store at most 2,147,483,647 seconds after the epoch, which is 03:14:07 UTC on 19 January 2038. One more second causes integer overflow, flipping the sign bit to indicate a negative number. One fix is to store time in a signed 64-bit integer.

probes.question: Unix time is the number of seconds elapsed since which moment?

claims.claim: Unix time counts seconds since 1 January 1970 and is stored in a signed 32-bit integer
claims.quote: the number of seconds elapsed since the Unix epoch (00:00:00 UTC on 1 January 1970)

claims.claim: Maximum is 2,147,483,647 seconds after the epoch, 03:14:07 UTC on 19 January 2038 (answer: 19 January 2038)
One more second causes integer overflow, flipping the sign bit to indicate a negative number
claims.quote: inadvertently flipping the sign bit to indicate a negative number

claims.claim: One fix is to store time in a signed 64-bit integer
claims.quote: Modern systems and software updates address this problem by using signed 64-bit integers

claims.claim: Probe 1 answer: Unix time counts from 00:00:00 UTC on 1 January 1970
Probe 2 answer: January 2038 is the limit of a signed 32-bit Unix time
